name: Angola

findings.summary: Ericsson completed modernising Unitel's core network with its dual-mode 5G Core, IMS and cloud-native infrastructure, letting 4G and 5G run on one platform; this follows a 2021 three-year Ericsson framework for radio and core upgrades.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third pole. TelecomTV and Connecting Africa likely both relay the same Ericsson release; ITWeb (2021) is independent reporting of the April 2021 Ericsson radio-and-core framework at 400+ sites. Tier 5 because the core transformation is reported complete. Value not disclosed; Unitel's US$25m 2021 upgrade budget not explicitly tied to Ericsson.

findings.summary: Unitel signed a three-year partnership agreement with Huawei covering its radio access network, transmission network and customer-experience management, described as also helping incubate 5G innovation.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: a partnership agreement with no value or deployment scale stated. Unitel appears multi-vendor (Ericsson also supplies RAN, AGO-001); the Huawei share of Unitel's RAN and whether the agreement was renewed after 2025 are unknown.

findings.summary: Nokia signed to build Africell's new Angolan network: AirScale Single RAN at up to 700 Luanda sites, cloud packet and voice core, microwave and IP transport, plus planning and managed care.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia is Finnish, so third pole. Both reports likely derive from the same Nokia announcement. Value undisclosed; current operational extent not checked. Africell Angola is the market's newest mobile entrant, so scale coded national though deployment is Luanda-centred.

findings.summary: NEC was contracted in 2014 as system supplier for Angola Cables' South Atlantic Cable System linking Luanda and Fortaleza, Brazil, at about US$160 million and 40 Tb/s design capacity; the cable was ready for service in 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: NEC is Japanese, so third pole under the equipment-vendor rule; Angola Cables (owner) is Angolan. US$160m is NEC's stated approximate contract value. Pre-2020 finding; current service not confirmed in this pass (still_current null).

findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Interior (Integrated Public Security Centres, CISP)
findings.financier: Chinese credit line (lender not named in opened sources)
findings.summary: Angola's first Integrated Public Security Centre opened in Luanda in January 2020 with over 700 cameras on a Chinese credit line; a Benguela centre followed in November 2020, funded via China and delivered by CEIEC with Huawei and Govec.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Controller coded as CEIEC (state-owned PRC integrator) with Huawei as equipment partner; no camera vendor is named in opened sources. Dates from the article URLs (January and November 2020); Benguela article gives 'Monday, November 9' without year. AidData relays that Phase 1 may have been Chinese-financed via a CEIEC contract (unverified there). Project plans extension to 16 other provinces.

findings.local_actor: Government of Angola (Ministry of the Interior)
findings.summary: China Eximbank signed a US$79.7 million loan with Angola's government for Phase 2 of the Public Security Project, to extend CCTV networks in Luanda and provincial centres with CEIEC and Huawei as implementing contractors.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 as a closed loan agreement; AidData gives no completion status. Single opened source, so uncorroborated. Linked to AGO-005 as the same programme's second phase.

findings.summary: Angola's state national data centre and unified government cloud, about US$90 million combined, was some 75% built in November 2025 with a 336-rack modular design; the ministry announced its launch in April 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: State owner-operator, so domestic. Builder, equipment vendor and financier not named; the US$300m World Bank PADA programme is mentioned but not tied to the centre. Tier 4 (construction well advanced); whether it is operational at scale was not confirmed. Both sources are the same outlet.

findings.controller: UAE Artificial Intelligence Office (Prime Minister's Office)
findings.summary: Angola's Institute for Administrative Modernization signed an MoU with the UAE's AI Office covering policy exchange, algorithms for intelligent public services, joint research and training; IMA is drafting a national AI strategy for public services.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded under models as the nearest layer for government AI adoption; no specific model or provider is named, so base_model null. Same article reports an Angolan delegation shown Huawei Atlas 900 infrastructure at Huawei Connect 2025 (not coded: a visit, not adoption).

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or export-licence reporting surfaced in data-centre or AI searches; no dedicated silicon search
